title: AI in Finance Atlas
intro: The models, risk engines, copilots and agent payment rails behind AI in financial services, and the rules that govern them.
initiativesHeading: How the world’s largest companies are using AI in finance

layers.name: Models & AI platforms
layers.description: The foundation-model labs and cloud AI platforms that banks, fintechs and crypto firms build on. Most financial institutions access models through a cloud platform with enterprise controls rather than directly, and model choice is increasingly a procurement and risk decision.
watch: Enterprise and financial-services deals with model labs
Data residency, private deployment and audit controls
Model pricing, rate limits and deprecation schedules
Finance-specific models, agents and connectors

layers.name: Risk, fraud & compliance AI
layers.description: AI that decides whether money should move: fraud scoring, AML and transaction monitoring, identity and KYC, credit underwriting and compliance automation. It is the most mature use of AI in finance and the most scrutinised by supervisors.
watch: Fraud and scam losses, especially authorised push payment fraud
Explainability and model risk management expectations
Consolidation: networks and PSPs buying fraud-AI vendors
Agent-initiated transactions changing fraud signals

layers.name: Investment, research & banking copilots
layers.description: AI assistants and agents for analysts, bankers, advisers and finance teams: research and diligence search, document drafting, data terminals with AI, and firm-wide LLM platforms inside banks.
watch: Firm-wide assistant rollouts and measured productivity gains
Licensing of premium data and news for AI use
Agentic workflows replacing analyst tasks
Client-facing advice and suitability rules

layers.name: Agentic commerce & payments
layers.description: The rails that let AI agents shop and pay on a user's behalf: card-network agent programmes with agentic tokens, checkout protocols between AI apps and merchants, and PSP toolkits. The open questions are identity, consent, liability and disputes when an agent pays.
watch: Agent identity and verifiable user consent
Tokenised credentials scoped to an agent
Checkout protocols between AI apps and merchants
Dispute and chargeback rules for agent purchases

layers.name: AI × crypto
layers.description: Where AI agents meet onchain money: HTTP-native stablecoin payments for agents, agent wallets with spending policies, onchain agent platforms and decentralised AI networks, plus AI used in crypto compliance and security.
watch: x402 and other machine-to-machine payment standards
Agent wallets: custody, spending limits and key management
Volume that is real usage versus incentives
AI in blockchain analytics, AML and smart-contract security

layers.name: Regulation & supervision
layers.description: Rules and supervisory guidance that govern AI in financial services: risk-based AI laws, model risk management, consumer protection and fair lending, and sandboxes where firms test AI with supervisors.
watch: EU AI Act obligations for high-risk uses such as credit scoring
Supervisory statements on generative AI and agents
Fair lending, explainability and adverse-action notices
AI sandboxes and live testing programmes
